key_insight: AnchorSeg disentangles semantic reasoning from spatial localization by replacing the single implicit segmentation token with a language-grounded bank of query anchors and treating mask generation as a structured conditional generation over image tokens. This explicit separation lets the model better interpret complex, implicit textual queries and produce more precise pixel-level masks.
problem_solved: Existing reasoning segmentation models compress both 'what to segment' and 'where to segment' into one <SEG> token, limiting interpretability and accuracy for complex, implicit language queries; AnchorSeg addresses this by providing structured, language-grounded query banks that explicitly ground reasoning into spatial predictions.
method: Introduce a bank of language-grounded query anchors that each encode aspects of the textual query, instead of a single <SEG> token.
Reformulate segmentation as a structured conditional generation process over image tokens, where anchors guide spatial grounding and mask synthesis separately from semantic reasoning.
Train the system to map language anchors to spatial token responses and compose them into precise pixel-level masks, improving modularity and interpretability.
impact: Makes reasoning segmentation more accurate, interpretable, and modular — enabling practitioners to debug, extend, and adapt models for complex multimodal queries and downstream tasks like VQA, robotics perception, and fine-grained scene understanding.

paper_title: AnchorSeg: Language Grounded Query Banks for Reasoning Segmentation
paper_authors: Rui Qian, Chuanhang Deng, Qiang Huang, Jian Xiong, Mingxuan Li
